title: Speaking & Writing
subject: Bahasa Inggris
prerequisites: Peserta didik telah mempelajari kosakata tambahan tentang pakaian dan memahami teks tentang berbelanja pakaian.
resources: Sumber Belajar:  Rise Up! Teens! Student Book 1, page 54-55
Laptop/ komputer, pengeras suara, projector, PPT
learningModel: Discovery Learning, Task-Based Learning, Tatap Muka.
approach: Peserta didik diajak untuk fokus dan saksama saat menyimak audio, mengamati detail gambar/komik, dan memperhatikan struktur bahasa yang digunakan.
Peserta didik menghubungkan materi pembelajaran dengan pengalaman dan kehidupan nyata mereka, sehingga pembelajaran terasa relevan dan bermanfaat.
Pembelajaran dikemas dalam aktivitas yang menyenangkan seperti permainan tebak hobi, kerja kelompok, penggunaan komik strip, dan survei interaktif.
objectives: Learners will be able to speak and write about liking and disliking certain clothes, and say why they are suitable or unsuitable (too + adjective / adjective + enough).
Learners will reflect on their own opinions about appearance, personality, and body image.
Learners will learn to have confidence and self-esteem.

details: Greet the students and ask about their feelings. For example: “How are you feeling today?” or “How would you describe your mood in one word?”
The teacher introduces himself/herself in front of the class.
Get to know the students by using the letter game.
The teacher writes down his/her name on the board (e.g. Susan)
Ask the student if their name starts with the shown letter (e.g. starts with S) and then they must stand up and introduce themselves. Continue with other letters.
Other alternatives to get to know the students: hot potato and throw the ball.
Ask students to look at Student Book page 54.

First, the teacher reads the questions and answers in the speech bubbles at the top of the page aloud for the students to hear (e.g. “Do you like this floral shirt?” – “Yes, I do. I think it’s big enough.” / “No, I don’t. I think it’s too small.”).
Next, the teacher asks everyone to read the speech bubbles aloud as a class.
Then, ask students to ask and answer the questions, in pairs.
Model to the students how the questions can be changed by changing some of the key vocabulary, e.g. “Do you like these striped socks?” – “No, I don’t. I think they’re too long.”

Now, put them in different pairs and ask them to substitute some of the key vocabulary in the questions so they can practice asking about different things. This can be repeated several times by putting students into different pairs.
To finish the speaking activity, elicit responses from some students by asking the questions in the speech bubbles with the original vocabulary, and also with some substituted vocabulary.

Check the Teacher’s Guide to see further explanation about the Language Box (meaning, form, use, common mistakes): too comes before the adjective (too big = a problem), enough comes after the adjective (big enough = OK), and plural items such as pants, shorts, and jeans use “they’re”.
Ask students to look at Speaking and Writing B on Student Book page 54. Put students in pairs and ask them to look at pictures 1-8 and write down the clothing the children are wearing.
Read the model question and answer on the left of the pictures and drill them as a whole class, e.g. “Do you like Max’s blue shorts?” – “No, I don’t. I think they’re too long.”

Ask students to take turns asking and answering questions about the children in pictures 1-8, following the model and the Language Box at the bottom of the page, and to write the questions and answers in their notebooks.
Students who are confident can add “I think” to their answers; students who need support can use the basic answer, e.g. “Yes, I do. It’s long enough.”
After 8-10 minutes, elicit example questions and answers from the class and write them on the board. Answers will vary, but they should follow the pattern in the Language Box.
Read some of the correct sentences aloud together as a class.
This is an additional activity for further practice if there is time.
Ask students to look back at the children on Student Book page 51.

Put students in pairs and ask them to ask and answer questions about these children, following the same question and answer model shown on Student Book page 54 (e.g. “Do you like Jenny’s long floral skirt?” – “Yes, I do. I think it’s long enough.”).
Give around 8-10 minutes for this task.
For an extra challenge, if students don’t like something about the clothes, they can say what they would change and why.
Elicit some answers from pairs of students.
Direct the students to look at the picture on page 55 and ask them “What can you see on the page?” to elicit some answers.

Next, tell students to read the text about the Teen Value (Personal Development & Self-Management: having confidence and self-esteem). They can read it silently, or put them in pairs to share reading the text aloud together, sentence by sentence.
Elicit from students, “What is the key focus of this Teen Corner page?”, and “Why do you think this skill (or value) is important?”
Note: the instructions for activity A should be given the week before this lesson, so students can prepare.

Students do one of the following: 1. search online OR take photos of their own clothes; 2. create a slide presentation of the pictures OR print them; 3. bring two to three pieces of their favorite clothes to school.
In class, ask students to sit in groups of three or four and show each other the pictures of their clothes or their real clothes.
If students have not prepared before the lesson, give them 5-10 minutes to draw their favorite clothes.
Encourage students to say one sentence about each item, e.g. “This is my blue hoodie. I like it because it is comfortable.”
Ask students to look at activity B. Read the instructions and questions aloud together as a class, and ask some instruction-checking questions.
Students write their own answers about their own clothes, but they can work in pairs so they can help each other.
Show some model answers before they start, e.g. “I like these clothes because they are comfortable and look nice.” / “I feel happy and confident when I wear my favorite clothes.”
Give students around 10 minutes to complete the activity, then elicit some answers from the class.
Ask students to look at activity C. Read the instructions and questions aloud together as a class.
Put students in pairs. They should draw and write about their own idea for a school uniform, but they can work together to help each other with ideas.

Show an example to guide students, e.g. “The girl’s uniform is a dark blue school jacket, a blue-and-white checked skirt, a light blue shirt, and black shoes. I like this uniform because it is simple and comfortable.”
Give students around 10 minutes to complete the activity.
Then put students in new pairs to show each other their uniform pictures and read their sentences aloud.
Ask some students to stand in front of the class and present their uniform ideas.
Wrap up the class by highlighting that everyone looks different and that being confident about ourselves is important. Remind students to always speak kindly about other people’s appearance.
Conclude the lesson, give feedback, and appreciation toward the student(s) / the whole class. Dismiss the class.

assessment: Asesmen formatif: unjuk kerja speaking berpasangan (kelancaran, ketepatan, keberanian).
Produk tulisan sederhana sesuai model di Student Book (struktur & kosakata unit).
Umpan balik teman sebaya dan guru terhadap hasil speaking/writing.
reflectionStudent: Apa hal baru yang kamu pelajari hari ini?
Bagian mana yang paling mudah dan paling sulit bagimu? Mengapa?
Kalimat bahasa Inggris apa yang sudah bisa kamu ucapkan dengan percaya diri?
Apa yang akan kamu lakukan untuk berlatih di rumah?
reflectionTeacher: Apakah tujuan pembelajaran tercapai? Bukti apa yang menunjukkannya?
Kegiatan mana yang paling efektif dan mana yang perlu diperbaiki?
Berapa persen instruksi kelas yang disampaikan dalam bahasa Inggris?
Peserta didik mana yang memerlukan pendampingan atau pengayaan?
